questions.q: A person sitting inside an elevator performs a weighing experiment with an object of mass 50 kg . Suppose that the variation of the height $y$ (in m ) of the elevator, from the ground, with time $t$ (in s ) is given by $y=8\left[1+\sin \left(\frac{2 \pi t}{T}\right)\right]$, where $T=40 \pi \mathrm{~s}$. Taking acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$, the maximum variation of the object's weight (in N ) as observed in the experiment is _______ .
questions.solution:
$y=8+8 \sin \frac{2 \pi t}{T}$
With respect to elevator, variation in weight will be
$\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{W}=\mathrm{m}(\Delta \mathrm{a})_{\max } \\ & \Delta \mathrm{W}=\mathrm{m} \times 2 \omega^2 \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$
Here elevator is performing SHM
$\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{W}=2 \mathrm{~m} \times\left(\frac{2 \pi}{\mathrm{~T}}\right)^2 \times \mathrm{A} \mathrm{N} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{W}=2 \times 50 \times\left(\frac{2 \pi}{40 \pi}\right)^2 \times 8 \mathrm{~N} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{~W}=2 \times 50 \times \frac{1}{400} \times 8 \mathrm{~N} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{~W}=\frac{800}{400} \mathrm{~N}=2 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: One end of a horizontal uniform beam of weight $W$ and length $L$ is hinged on a vertical wall at point $O$ and its other end is supported by a light inextensible rope. The other end of the rope is fixed at point $Q$, at a height $L$ above the hinge at point $O$. A block of weight $\alphaW$ is attached at the point $P$ of the beam, as shown in the figure (not to scale). The rope can sustain a maximum tension of $\left(2\sqrt{2}\right)W$. Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
options: The vertical component of reaction force at $O$ does not depend on $\alpha$.
The horizontal component of reaction force at $O$ is equal to $W$ for $\alpha = 0 . 5$.
The tension in the rope is $2W$ for $\alpha = 0 . 5$.
questions.solution:
$∵$ Rod is in equilibrium, net torque on the rod about $O$ will be zero.

$W\left(\dfrac{l}{2}\right) + \alphaW\left(l\right) = \dfrac{T}{\sqrt{2}}l$

$⇒ \dfrac{W}{2} + \alphaW = \dfrac{T}{\sqrt{2}} ⇒ T = \sqrt{2}W\left(\alpha + 0 . 5\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

Now checking options-

(A)

Force balance on rod,

${N}_{v} + \dfrac{T}{\sqrt{2}} = W + \alphaW$

$⇒ {N}_{v} = \left(W + \alphaW\right) - \left(\dfrac{W}{2} + \alphaW\right)$

$⇒ {N}_{v} = \dfrac{W}{2}$

Hence, option (A) is correct.

(B) Write horizontal force equation,

${N}_{H} = \dfrac{T}{\sqrt{2}} ⇒ {N}_{H} = W\left(\alpha + 0 . 5\right)$

If $\alpha = 0 . 5$, then,

${N}_{H} = W$ and $T = \sqrt{2}W$

Hence, option (B) is correct.

(D) $∴$ Maximum Tension of string $= 2\sqrt{2}W$

So, to break.

$T > 2\sqrt{2}W ⇒ \sqrt{2}W\left(\alpha + 0 . 5\right) > 2\sqrt{2}W ⇒ \alpha > 1 . 5$

So, string will break.

option (D) correct.

questions.q:
A block of mass $2M$ is attached to a massless spring with spring-constant $k .$ This block is connected to two other blocks of masses $M$ and $2M$ using two massless pulleys and strings. The accelerations of the blocks are ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}$ as shown in figure. The system is released from rest with the spring in its unstretched state. The maximum extension of the spring is ${x}_{0} .$ Which of the following option(s) is/are correct?
[ $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity. Neglect friction]
options: When spring achieves an extension of $\dfrac{{x}_{0}}{2}$ for the first time, the speed of the block connected to the spring is $3g\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{5k}}$
At an extension of $\dfrac{{x}_{0}}{4}$ of the spring, the magnitude of acceleration of the block connected to the spring is $\dfrac{3g}{10}$
questions.solution:
Using string constraint
${a}_{1} = \dfrac{{a}_{2} + {a}_{3}}{2}$
$⇒ 2{a}_{1} = {a}_{2} + {a}_{3}$
${a}_{1} - {a}_{3} = {a}_{2} - {a}_{1} ⇒ \left(C\right)$ is correct.
for other options use $m$ equivalent

Equivalent mass
Or Reduced mass
${m}_{eq} = \dfrac{2{m}_{1} \times {m}_{2}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2}}$ (for a two-mass system)
$= \dfrac{2\left(2m\right) \times m}{2m + m} = \dfrac{4m}{3}$
$⇒ T = \left(\dfrac{4m}{3}\right) . g$
$∴ 2T = 2 . \dfrac{4mg}{3} = \left(\dfrac{8m}{3}\right)g$
$⇒ {m}_{eq} = \dfrac{8m}{3}$

Using mechanical energy conservation
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2} = \dfrac{8mg}{3}{x}_{0}$
${x}_{0} = \dfrac{16mg}{3k} ⇒ \left(A\right)$ is incorrect
Option $\left(B\right) ⇒ {V}_{\dfrac{{x}_{0}}{2}} = {V}_{max} = \dfrac{{x}_{0}}{2}\omega = \dfrac{{x}_{0}}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{2m + \dfrac{8m}{3}}} = \dfrac{{x}_{0}}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{14m}} = g\sqrt{\dfrac{32}{21k}}$
Option $\left(D\right) ⇒ {a}_{\dfrac{{x}_{0}}{4}} = \dfrac{{x}_{0}}{4}{\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{{x}_{0}}{4}\dfrac{3k}{14m} = \dfrac{3k{x}_{0}}{42m} = \dfrac{8g}{21}$
For a simple harmonic motion ${x}_{0} ⇒$ maximum displacement from extreme to extreme
$⇒ {x}_{0} = 2A ⇒ A = \dfrac{{x}_{0}}{2}$
and $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k}{14m}}$
$∴ {v}_{max} = A . \omega$
and $a = {\omega}^{2} . x$

questions.q:
A block of weight $100N$ is suspended by copper and steel wires of same cross-sectional area $0.5c{m}^{2}$ and, length $\sqrt{3}m$ and 1m, respectively. Their other ends are fixed on a ceiling as shown in figure. The angles subtended by copper and steel wires with ceiling are ${30}^{o} and {60}^{o},$ respectively. If elongation in copper wire is $\left(\Delta{l}_{C}\right)$ and elongation in steel wire is $\left(\Delta{l}_{S}\right),$ then the ratio $\dfrac{\Delta{l}_{C}}{\Delta{l}_{S}}$ is _____.
[Young's modulus for copper and steel are $1 \times {10}^{11}N / {m}^{2} and 2 \times {10}^{11}N / {m}^{2}$ respectively]
questions.solution:
2.00

Resolving in components
$⇒ ∑ {F}_{x} = 0$
$⇒ {T}_{S}cos60 = {T}_{C} ⋅ cos30$
$⇒ {T}_{S} ⋅ \dfrac{1}{2} = {T}_{C} ⋅ \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$⇒ {T}_{S} = \sqrt{3} ⋅ {T}_{C}$
$\dfrac{\Delta{l}_{C}}{\Delta{l}_{S}} = \left(\dfrac{{T}_{C} ⋅ {l}_{C}}{\dfrac{{T}_{S} ⋅ {l}_{S}}{{Y}_{S}}}\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{\Delta{l}_{C}}{\Delta{l}_{S}} = \left(\dfrac{{T}_{C}}{{T}_{S}}\right)\left(\dfrac{{l}_{C}}{{l}_{S}}\right)\left(\dfrac{{Y}_{S}}{{Y}_{C}}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{1}\right)\left(\dfrac{2 \times {10}^{11}}{1 \times {10}^{11}}\right) = 2$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is initially at rest at the origin. It is subjected to a force and starts moving along the x - axis. Its kinetic energy changes with time as $dK / dt = \gammat,$ where $\gamma$ is a positive constant of appropriate dimensions. Which of the following statements is (are) true?
options: The force applied on the particle is constant
The speed of the particle is proportional to time
The distance of the particle from the origin increases linearly with time
Since force is constant, it is conservative.
questions.solution:
Given the change in kinetic energy$\dfrac{dk}{dt} = \gammat$.

Kinetic energy is expressed as $k = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$.
$∴ \dfrac{dk}{dt} = mv\dfrac{dv}{dt} = \gammat$
Integrating the above relation,

$m{∫}_{0}^{v}vdv = \gamma{∫}_{0}^{t}tdt$
$\dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{\gamma{t}^{2}}{2}$
$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma}{m}}t; υ ∝ t$ ... (i)
$a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma}{m}} = constant$
Since $F = ma$
$∴ F = m\sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma}{m}} = \sqrt{\gammam} = constant$

questions.q: A solid horizontal surface is covered with a thin layer of oil. A rectangular block of mass $m = 0.4kg$ is at rest on this surface. An impulse of $1.0Ns$ is applied to the block at time $t = 0$ so that it starts moving along the x-axis with a velocity $v\left(t\right) = {v}_{0}{e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}$ , where ${v}_{0}$ is a constant and $τ = 4$ . The displacement of the block, in meter, at $t = τ$ is __________. Take ${e}^{- 1} = 0.37$

$v = {v}_{0}{e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}$
${v}_{0} = \dfrac{J}{m} = 2.5m / s$

${∫}_{0}^{x}dx = {v}_{0}{∫}_{0}^{τ}{e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}dt$
$∫ {e}^{- x}dx = \dfrac{{e}^{- x}}{- 1}$
$x = {v}_{0}{\left[\dfrac{{e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}}{- \dfrac{1}{τ}}\right]}_{0}^{τ}$
$x = 2.5\left(- 4\right)\left({e}^{- 1} - {e}^{0}\right)$
$x = 25\left(- 4\right)\left(0.37 - 1\right)$
$x = 6.30$

questions.q: A particle, of mass ${10}^{- 3}kg$ and charge $1.0C$, is initially at rest. At time $t = 0$, the particle comes under the influence of an electric field $\overset{\to}{E}\left(t\right) = {E}_{0}sin\left(\omegat\right)\overset{^}{i}$ where ${E}_{0} = 1.0N{C}^{- 1}$ and $\omega = {10}^{3}rad{s}^{- 1}$. Consider the effect of only the electrical force on the particle. Then the maximum speed, in $m{s}^{- 1}$, attained by the particle at subsequent times is ____________.
questions.solution:
$m = {10}^{- 3}kg, q = 1C, t = 0$
Force on particle will be
$F = qE = q{E}_{0}sin\left(\omegat\right)$
At ${v}_{max}, F = 0$ $⇒ q{E}_{0}sin ⁡ \omega{t}_{o} = 0$
$⇒ \omega{t}_{o} = \pi$
$F = q{E}_{0}sin ⁡ \omegat$
$\dfrac{dv}{dt} = q\dfrac{{E}_{0}}{m}sin\left(\omegat\right)$
${∫}_{0}^{v}dv = {∫}_{0}^{\pi ∕ \omega}\dfrac{q{E}_{0}}{m}sin\left(\omegat\right)dt$
$v - 0 = \dfrac{q{E}_{0}}{m\omega}{\left[- cos\left(\omegat\right)\right]}_{0}^{\pi ∕ \omega}$
$v - 0 = \dfrac{q{E}_{0}}{m\omega}\left[\left(- cos\left(\pi\right)\right) - \left(- cos\left(0\right)\right)\right]$
$v = \dfrac{1 \times 1}{m\omega} \times 2 = 2 m {s}^{- 1}$

Now consider a smooth slot along a diameter of a disc of radius $R$ rotating counter-clockwise with a constant angular speed $\omega$ about its vertical axis through its center. questions.q: A uniform wooden stick of mass 1.6 kg and length $l$ rests in an inclined manner on a smooth, vertical wall of height h $\left(< l\right)$ such that a small portion of the stick extends beyond the wall. The reaction force of the wall on the stick is perpendicular to the stick. The stick makes an angle of ${30}^{o}$ with the wall and the bottom of the stick is on a rough floor. questions.solution:
Force equation in x-direction,
${N}_{1}cos ⁡ {30}^{o} - f = 0$ ....(i)
Force equation in y-direction,
${N}_{1}sin ⁡ {30}^{o} + {N}_{2} - mg = 0$ ....(ii)
Torque equation about O,
$mg\dfrac{l}{2}cos ⁡ {60}^{o} - {N}_{1}\dfrac{h}{cos ⁡ {30}^{o}} = 0$ ...(iii)
Also, given ${N}_{1} = {N}_{2}$ .....(iv)
[Note taking reaction from floor as normal reaction only]

$\dfrac{h}{l} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{16}$ and $f = \dfrac{16\sqrt{3}}{3}$

questions.q: A bob of mass $m$, suspended by a string of length ${l}_{1}$, is given a minimum velocity required to complete a full circle in the vertical plane. At the highest point, it collides elastically with another bob of mass $m$, suspended by a string of length ${l}_{2}$, which is initially at rest. Both the strings are mass-less and inextensible. If the second bob, after collision acquires the minimum speed required to complete a full circle in the vertical plane, the ratio $\dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{l}_{2}}$ is
questions.solution:
As shown in the figure shown above, the minimum speed required by the bob of mass $m$ attached to the string of length ${l}_{1}$ in order to complete the full circle is $\sqrt{5g{l}_{1}}$.

When the bob goes to the highest point, its speed becomes $\sqrt{g{l}_{1}}$. Here, it strikes with the identical mass, which is tied to the string of length ${l}_{2}$. The speed delivered to the object is $\sqrt{g{l}_{1}}$. This should be equal to $\sqrt{5g{l}_{2}}$ so that this bob could complete a full circle.   
$\sqrt{g{l}_{1}} = \sqrt{5g{l}_{2}}$
$⇒ g{l}_{1} = 5g{l}_{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{l}_{2}} = 5$
